model: q≥2,b≥1,0≤a≤b are integers; two groups of q labelled topics; b distinct unit customers per cross-group pair and a per within-group pair; m=q+1 sequential unit providers with every ordered history, legal repetition and weak tie retained.

mathematical_checks.claim: Single-use terminal payoff and every genuine subgame continuation floor
mathematical_checks.derivation: Put S=qb+(q−1)a and L=S−qb/2. If terminal z_v=1, the other q actions give u_v=Σ_w μ_vw/(1+z_w)≥S−(b/2)Σ_w z_w=L, using 1/(1+k)≥1−k/2 for integer k≥0 and μ_vw≤b. At any history before a move at most q topics have appeared, so a fresh topic exists among 2q labels. Force it in the same complete strategy. Either it remains single-use or a later mover repeats it. In the latter case the forced mover and that later mover have identical terminal payoff; the later mover belongs to a strictly deeper genuine subgame and the backward induction floor applies. Current optimality then gives every still-to-move actual player at least L. The same two cases prove L_h(v)≥L for every previously unused forced v without requiring that forced move itself to be optimal.

mathematical_checks.claim: Exact root threshold uses the existential construction only for the opposite inequality
mathematical_checks.derivation: The source controller, with the specified most-recent-group tie rule and complete backward-induction exits after the first repeat, supplies a complete child SPE after every root v. Its q followers use all q opposite-group labels once. The root earns qb/2+(q−1)a=L. Hence L_empty(v)≤L for each v; the universal child floor gives equality and Θ_empty=L. An arbitrary group tie rule would not give this witness, and no such relaxation is used.

mathematical_checks.claim: Independent algebra for the true coverage optimum
mathematical_checks.derivation: A support may be enlarged to m=q+1 distinct labels, leaving x+y=q−1 unused labels in the two groups. Its uncovered customer count is a[binom(x,2)+binom(y,2)]+bxy=a binom(q−1,2)+(b−a)xy. Since b≥a, the minimum is attained by x=0 or y=0. Subtracting from N=q²b+q(q−1)a gives OPT=q²b+(q−1)(q+2)a/2. This also handles a=b and a=0.

mathematical_checks.claim: The same actual path admits the needed ordering of an optimal support
mathematical_checks.derivation: Assign the m distinct optimal labels backward from position m. At step i there remain i candidates while the actual prefix h_i contains at most i−1 distinct labels, so one candidate is fresh. Thus Σ_i L_hi(T_i)≥mL. Actual welfare is Σ_i u_i≥mL, and 2mL−OPT=qb+(q−1)(3q+2)a/2>0, so Σ_i L_hi(T_i)≥OPT−W. The independent full-continuation recursion supplies L_hi(T_i)≤Θ_hi≤u_i(actual), which closes half for this family.

mathematical_checks.claim: All complete root SPE are optimal when a>0
mathematical_checks.derivation: A new repeater receives at most S/2<L, contradicting the actual mover floor; root outcomes therefore have distinct labels. When a=b every m-label support has the same coverage. For 0<a<b, F(s)=S−[b(q+1−s)+a(s−1)]/2 strictly increases with the mover’s final own-group count. At a no-repeat prefix x>y≥1 with x+y≤q, joining the majority produces own-group count q+1−y; joining the minority gives y+1 if x≥y+2 or at most q−y if x=y+1, both strictly smaller. For x>y=0 and x≥2, the majority route reaches q and a minority deviation leaves the deviator alone. Balanced prefixes choose either next majority. Root-prefix cases therefore end at counts (q,1) or (1,q), attaining the optimum just calculated.

mathematical_checks.claim: The a=0 weak-tie boundary also preserves all-SPE optimality
mathematical_checks.derivation: Any repeated label earns at most L, strictly less when an opposite-group label is present or the label appears at least three times. Actual movers are all at least L. Consequently a root outcome with a repeat uses only one group and each repeated label occurs exactly twice. If a second repeat action were contemplated, there is an earlier label of count at least two. Switching to a fresh opposite-group topic produces, in every genuine continuation, a single-use deviating label: copying any label after both groups appear would be strictly below L for its new copier. The deviator earns bΣ_w1/(1+z_w)>qb−(b/2)Σ_w z_w≥qb/2=L because an existing z_w≥2 makes the integer bound strict. Thus the second repeat is impossible. With q+1 actions, a one-group outcome uses all q labels and covers every cross customer. If both groups occur, no copies can be added and the majority argument gives (q,1) or (1,q). Every case attains OPT.

mathematical_checks.claim: The aggregate-floor counterexample attacks a different universal statement
mathematical_checks.derivation: The fully described 36-customer three-player instance has a complete SPE with payoff (10,12,12), W=34, θ_3=12 and OPT=36. Thus W≥3θ_3 fails, while 2W≥OPT holds. Its customers include four-label membership types, so it is outside the two-label-membership family reviewed here. It neither refutes the family theorem nor supplies the missing general same-path payment inequality.

edge_review.reason: The source provides an attaining credible child and an optimal support. It does not alone prove the all-children lower bound or universal all-SPE optimality; contribution.remaining accurately names the independent target proof obligations.

The proved family theorem supplies the full family-specific route5 payment step. The target resource concerns general catalogues, so contribution rather than whole_result is required and is present. The original complete ordered-history model is retained.

open_obligations: For a general common catalogue, the actual-path optimal-position payment Σ_i L_hi(T_i)≥OPT−W remains a separate obligation.
The reviewed family theorem does not determine exact L_h(A) for previously used labels or all nonempty-history Θ_h.
The general exact-six half-cover target and open SUMmin budget are not promoted by this restricted-family theorem.
verdict: No mathematical or scope correction is required in the two current contribution edges. The universal family theorem and its root-attainment source have distinct, correctly recorded proof roles.
